subject: MAP: POC access audit — API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@helioshealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft + POC infra asks

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the MAP you shared last week — Sam from Helios infra here. We're ready to start the environment setup for the POC and want to confirm the minimum items your team needs in the MAP to unblock the evaluation. Specifically:

- API credentials / service account provisioning model (team vs project keys)
- Redwood org invite / admin roles and recommended org settings
- IP allowlist requirements (we'll need an explicit list to configure our outbound proxies)
- VPC peering requirements: supported cloud regions, required CIDR ranges, and any routing/NAT notes

Can you confirm these items and share a short checklist we can run through with our infra team? We can provide AWS account IDs and VPC IDs once we confirm the expected CIDR/IP ranges.

Attached: Helios_MAP_v1.docx (outline of evaluation success criteria)

Ideal timeline: we want to spin up the POC infra by next week (targeting 2027-04-08). Is that achievable?

Thanks,
Sam Patel
Lead Infrastructure Engineer
Helios Health

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.d@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.b@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + POC infra asks

Sam — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned on the items and I've looped in Priyom (infra/ops) to own the technical checklist and Lauren for timeline/credits. High level answers upfront:

- API provisioning: we provide short-lived API keys scoped to an "evaluation" org by default; for production you can request service-account style keys tied to an org admin. For the POC we can create two keys: one owner-admin key (team scope) and one read-only key for metrics.
- Org setup: invite process is email-based; we'll create an org placeholder and invite your org admin. We recommend enabling SSO later but not required for POC.
- IP allowlist: we need outbound CIDR blocks (IPv4) you'll allow; alternatively we can provide a small set of egress IPs if you want fixed endpoints.
- VPC peering: we support AWS VPC peering (us-west-2, us-east-1) and Azure peering via service endpoints. We'll need your VPC ID, account ID, and the target Redwood VPC info (we'll share on request).

Next steps I propose:
1) Priyom to send a short technical checklist and required firewall rules (ports, CIDR format).
2) Helios to send AWS account ID, VPC ID, and preferred peering windows.
3) We provision org and API keys, then do a joint peering runbook during the agreed window.

I've attached our MAP template (redwood-map-template.xlsx) and set an internal note to prioritize this. Priyom — can you pick this up and outline the sequence + estimated effort?

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.d@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@helioshealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP draft + POC infra asks

Hey all — Priyom here with the technical checklist we use for MAP-driven POCs. I kept this short so your infra team can action quickly. Attached: poc-network-checklist.pdf

Minimum technical items for Redwood-hosted POC (stepwise):

1) Org & Identity
   - Provide one primary org admin email for Helios. We'll send an invite and mark the account as "evaluation".
   - Optional: if you want SSO, provide IdP metadata; we'll schedule that after POC spin-up.

2) API keys
   - We'll create two keys: eval-admin (full scope, rotates every 30d) and eval-readonly. Keys delivered via secure share link.

3) IP allowlist / egress
   - Preferred: provide a list of outbound IPv4 CIDR ranges (e.g., 203.0.113.0/24). If you cannot provide ranges, request our fixed egress set (we provide 3 IPs for eval).
   - Required ports: 443 (HTTPS) outbound. If you have strict egress filtering, allow TLS to our egress IPs on 443.

4) VPC peering (optional but recommended for latency-sensitive workloads)
   - Provide: AWS account ID, VPC ID, primary subnet CIDR (e.g., 10.10.0.0/16), and desired peering window.
   - Notes: We do not require overlapping CIDRs; if overlaps exist we can use a NAT-based proxy. Peering typically takes 1–3 hours including routing updates.

5) Test plan and smoke checks (will run jointly):
   - API handshake + simple generation (100 tokens)
   - Latency test from a warm instance (p50/p95)
   - KV cache validation if using embeddings or chat histories

Estimated effort: 1 business day of coordinated work (provision + smoke test) assuming we have AWS/VPC details and a 2–4 hour peering window.

Questions for Helios: please send AWS account ID(s), VPC ID(s), preferred peering windows (UTC), and the primary infra contact.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Sam — quick commercial note so we're aligned on the close timeline. We can support an accelerated POC and provide 14 days of evaluation credits (covers token usage and a limited Dedicated burst for testing). To keep the MAP tight, here's a proposed set of milestones and target close dates:

- MAP sign-off (mutual acceptance of success criteria): 2027-04-07
- POC infra ready (API keys + peering): 2027-04-09
- Validation window (customer runs tests): 2027-04-09 — 2027-04-16
- POC review & acceptance: 2027-04-19

If those dates look good, we'll add them to the MAP and I'll prepare the short mutual actions table (owners, due dates, acceptance criteria). Also note: if Helios needs a later finish date, we can extend the validation window but credits are time-bound to the first 14 days of activity.

Lauren Bishop
